column3: The Hebrew says “after her dismissal,” without explicitly naming Moses as the one who sent her back.
The Hebrew simply says “he said,” rather than explicitly “sent word.”
The Hebrew says they asked each other about their welfare, rather than simply greeted each other.
The final rescue is literally “from under the hand of Egypt.”
The Hebrew leaves the arrogant actors and their victims as pronouns, without explicitly repeating Israel or saying “He did this.”
The Hebrew does not separately add “as judge” in the question.
The Hebrew uses the broader word “matter” and explicitly makes Moses the subject of “I judge.”
The Hebrew says “listen to my voice” and repeats God as the recipient of the matters.
The Hebrew retains the image of a way in which they should walk.
The Hebrew includes a direct instruction to lighten the burden from himself.
The Hebrew says they will come “to their place,” rather than explicitly “home.”
The Hebrew says he listened to his father-in-law’s “voice.”
The Hebrew says “he went to his land,” without repeating Jethro’s name or explicitly saying “returned.”
